types.oie_definition: An individual human being.
types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called individual, human, celebrity, public figure.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org Person class perfectly matches the OIE type definition and all mentions are specific instances of individuals.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: GovernmentOfficial
candidates.comment: A person holding an office in a government or public administration.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Journalist
candidates.comment: A person who writes or prepares news for publication or broadcast.

candidates.label: EnvironmentalPhenomenon
candidates.comment: A natural occurrence or observable fact related to the environment.

types.oie_definition: A large and permanent human settlement, typically with a defined administrative boundary.
types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and permanent human settlement, typically with a defined administrative boundary. Also called town, metropolis, urban area.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org City class perfectly matches the OIE type definition and the mentions are specific cities or a generic reference to one.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

types.oie_definition: A Uniform Resource Locator, which specifies the location of a resource on the internet and the mechanism for retrieving it.
types.embedding_query_text: URL: A Uniform Resource Locator, which specifies the location of a resource on the internet and the mechanism for retrieving it. Also called web address, link, website address.

chosen_type.label: URL
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org URL data type perfectly matches the OIE type definition and the mention is a valid URL string.

candidates.label: URL
candidates.comment: A data type representing a Uniform Resource Locator, which specifies the address of a resource on the internet. Also called web address, link, internet address. Examples: "https://schema.org", "ftp://example.com/file.zip", "mailto:info@example.com".

candidates.label: BreadcrumbList
candidates.comment: A BreadcrumbList is an ItemList representing a hierarchical navigation path, typically on a website, showing the user's current location relative to the site's structure. Also called navigation path, breadcrumbs, site path. Examples: Home > Products > Electronics > Televisions, Blog > Category > Post Title.

candidates.label: WebPage
candidates.comment: A single document or resource accessible via a web browser, typically part of a larger website. Also called web document, HTML page, internet page. Examples: a product page on an e-commerce site, a news article page, a contact us page.

candidates.label: WPFooter
candidates.comment: The bottom section of a web page, typically containing copyright information, contact details, and navigation links. Also called page footer, website footer, site bottom. Examples: the copyright notice at the bottom of a website, links to privacy policy and terms of service, social media icons in the footer.

candidates.label: WebSite
candidates.comment: A collection of related web pages and other items, typically served from a single domain. Also called website, internet site, web presence. Examples: schema.org, Wikipedia, The New York Times website.

types.oie_definition: A specific day of the calendar year.

candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Periodical
candidates.comment: A Periodical, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a publication issued in successive parts with numerical or chronological designations, intended to continue indefinitely. Also called serial publication, magazine, journal. Examples: The New Yorker magazine, a scholarly journal, a daily newspaper. Distinct from Book, which is a single, non-serial publication.

candidates.label: PublicationIssue
candidates.comment: A PublicationIssue is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or publication volume, often numbered and containing a grouping of works. Also called journal issue, magazine issue, periodical issue. Examples: "Nature" Vol. 500, Issue 1; "The New Yorker" October 26, 2023 issue; a specific issue of a scientific journal. Distinct from PublicationVolume, which is a larger grouping of issues.

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

types.oie_definition: A television program that consists of a sequence of episodes.
types.embedding_query_text: TV Series: A television program that consists of a sequence of episodes. Also called television show, TV show, series.

chosen_type.label: TVSeries
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org TVSeries class perfectly matches the OIE type definition and the mention is a specific television series.

candidates.label: TVEpisode
candidates.comment: A single installment of a television series, typically part of a season. Also called television episode, show episode, broadcast installment. Examples: 'The Pilot' episode of a new series, 'Episode 5 of Season 2' of a drama.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: TVSeries
candidates.comment: A creative work series dedicated to television broadcast and associated online delivery, comprising multiple seasons and episodes. Also called television show, TV program, broadcast series. Examples: 'Game of Thrones', 'The Office', 'Stranger Things'.

candidates.label: Series
candidates.comment: A general group of related items, which may or may not be of the same kind, forming a sequence or collection. Also called collection, sequence, set, installment. Examples: a book series, a lecture series, a product line, a collection of artworks. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is a series of creative works.

candidates.label: Episode
candidates.comment: An Episode is a CreativeWork representing a single installment of a media series, such as a TV show, radio program, or video game. Also called installment, segment, part. Examples: A single episode of a TV series, a chapter in a podcast, a level in a video game series.

types.oie_definition: A phrase or term used to describe the age or longevity of something.
types.embedding_query_text: Age Descriptor: A phrase or term used to describe the age or longevity of something. Also called age indicator, duration descriptor.

chosen_type.label: AgeQualifier
chosen_type.definition: A descriptive term or phrase indicating the age or longevity of an entity.
chosen_type.justification: No existing candidate represents an 'Age Descriptor' as a descriptive phrase; 'Age' is for numerical values, and 'Duration' is for periods.

candidates.label: Age
candidates.comment: The length of time that a person has lived, expressed as a numerical value.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: AdultOrientedEnumeration
candidates.comment: AdultOrientedEnumeration is an Enumeration of factors that make a product or content relevant or potentially restricted for adults only. Also called adult content classification, age restriction type, mature content indicator. Examples: `AdultSexualContent`, `ViolentContent`, `GamblingContent`.

candidates.label: Month
candidates.comment: One of the twelve periods of time into which a year is divided.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

types.oie_definition: An institution of higher education and research, which grants academic degrees in various subjects.
types.embedding_query_text: University: An institution of higher education and research, which grants academic degrees in various subjects. Also called college, academy, higher education institution.

chosen_type.label: CollegeOrUniversity
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org CollegeOrUniversity class perfectly matches the OIE type definition and the mention is a specific university.

candidates.label: CollegeOrUniversity
candidates.comment: A third-level educational institution providing higher education. Also called university, college, higher education institution. Examples: Harvard University, Oxford College, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Sorbonne University. Distinct from EducationalOrganization, which is a broader category for any educational body.

candidates.label: School
candidates.comment: An educational organization providing instruction to students, typically for primary or secondary education. Also called educational institution, academy, learning center, college. Examples: a public elementary school, a private high school, a vocational school, a university.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

candidates.label: HighSchool
candidates.comment: A HighSchool is an educational organization and civic structure providing secondary education. Also called secondary school, senior high, academy. Examples: Springfield High School, Northwood Academy, a local public high school.

types.oie_definition: The length of time that a person has lived or a thing has existed.
types.embedding_query_text: Age: The length of time that a person has lived or a thing has existed. Also called years old, lifespan.

chosen_type.label: Age
chosen_type.definition: The length of time that a person has lived, expressed as a numerical value.
chosen_type.justification: The vocabulary Age class perfectly matches the OIE type definition for the length of time a person has lived, expressed numerically.

candidates.label: Age
candidates.comment: The length of time that a person has lived, expressed as a numerical value.

candidates.label: Month
candidates.comment: One of the twelve periods of time into which a year is divided.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Temperature
candidates.comment: A measure of the warmth or coldness of an object or substance, typically expressed with a unit.

types.oie_definition: A day or period of celebration, typically for religious reasons or to mark a particular season or event.
types.embedding_query_text: Festival: A day or period of celebration, typically for religious reasons or to mark a particular season or event. Also called celebration, gala, fete.

chosen_type.label: Festival
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org Festival class perfectly matches the OIE type definition and the mention is a specific festival.

candidates.label: Festival
candidates.comment: A Festival is an Event that is a public celebration or series of special events. Also called celebration, gala, fete. Examples: A music festival, a film festival, a cultural heritage festival, a food and wine festival.

candidates.label: HolidayWeekend
candidates.comment: A period of several days including a public holiday, typically extending a weekend.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: DanceEvent
candidates.comment: A DanceEvent is a social gathering or organized occasion primarily focused on dancing. Also called dance party, ball, disco, social dance. Examples: A salsa night, a wedding reception with dancing, a school prom, a folk dance festival.

types.oie_definition: A geographical and administrative division within a country or state.
types.embedding_query_text: County: A geographical and administrative division within a country or state. Also called shire, province, region.

chosen_type.label: AdministrativeArea
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org AdministrativeArea class is the best fit, as a county is a type of geographical administrative division.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: SchoolDistrict
candidates.comment: An administrative area responsible for the organization and operation of public schools within its geographical boundaries. Also called education district, school system, local education authority. Examples: 'Los Angeles Unified School District', 'New York City Department of Education', 'Springfield School District 186'.

types.oie_definition: A specific number or amount of something.
types.embedding_query_text: Quantity: A specific number or amount of something. Also called amount, number, count.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org Quantity data type perfectly matches the OIE type definition and the mention is a specific amount.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: IncidentCount
candidates.comment: A numerical count of occurrences or events.

candidates.label: Temperature
candidates.comment: A measure of the warmth or coldness of an object or substance, typically expressed with a unit.

candidates.label: Percentage
candidates.comment: A rate, number, or amount expressed as a fraction of one hundred.

types.oie_definition: A general classification for a kind of place where events or activities are held.
types.embedding_query_text: Venue Type: A general classification for a kind of place where events or activities are held. Also called location type, facility type, event space type.

chosen_type.label: EventVenue
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org EventVenue class is the best fit, as 'stadium' is a type of location specifically designed for events.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: EventVenue
candidates.comment: An EventVenue is a CivicStructure that serves as a location for events. Also called venue, event space, performance hall. Examples: A concert hall, a stadium, a conference center, a community hall.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: ExhibitionEvent
candidates.comment: An ExhibitionEvent is an Event type focused on displaying items, such as at a museum, library, or tradeshow. Also called exhibit, show, display event. Examples: An art exhibition at a gallery, a historical display at a museum, a trade show for new technologies, a book fair.

types.oie_definition: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months, corresponding to the Earth's revolution around the sun.
types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months, corresponding to the Earth's revolution around the sun. Also called calendar year, annum.

chosen_type.label: CalendarYear
chosen_type.definition: A period of 365 or 366 days, typically starting from January 1st, corresponding to the Earth's revolution around the sun.
chosen_type.justification: No existing candidate directly represents 'Year' as a distinct type; 'Month' is too specific, and other duration types are not appropriate.

candidates.label: Month
candidates.comment: One of the twelve periods of time into which a year is divided.

candidates.label: HolidayWeekend
candidates.comment: A period of several days including a public holiday, typically extending a weekend.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.
